description: Where the agent looks first, by tier. Tier 1-2 sources can support a claim alone. Tier 3 can support descriptive claims and must be labeled. Tier 4 never supports a claim alone.

examples.name: OECD Health Statistics / Health at a Glance
European Observatory on Health Systems and Policies: Health Systems in Transition reviews
WHO/World Bank UHC Global Monitoring Report

2.label: Peer-reviewed research
2.notes: Prefer systematic reviews and studies published in the last 5 years. Record study design and data years. A study about a system that has since been reformed must say so.

3.label: Government and established independent research
examples: National ministries of health and statutory insurers
Commonwealth Fund (International Health Care System Profiles; Mirror, Mirror)
KFF, Health Foundation, Nuffield Trust, King's Fund, RAND
3.notes: Record funder or institutional stance in funding_note when relevant (e.g. advocacy organizations).

4.label: Other (news, reputable explainers)
4.notes: Only for very recent events not yet covered elsewhere, and only alongside a higher-tier source.
